data.name: Naafil
data.gender_notes: Naafil is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root n-f-l which means to give, to offer, or to add. In Islamic contexts, Naafil refers to acts of worship that are voluntary and not required by Islamic law. These acts are considered meritorious and serve to strengthen one's faith. The name Naafil carries the meaning “Superfluous, optional” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Naafil usually hope their child will grow to embody superfluous, optional and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Naafil total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_hindi.name: नाफ़ील
in_hindi.long_meaning: नाफ़िलात: वे कार्य जो अल्लाह के द्वारा अनिवार्य नहीं है, लेकिन अल्लाह ने हमें इन कार्यों की ओर हिदायत की है। अल्लाह ने कहा है: {फ़ ला वरब्बका ला योमिनु नासु वला यत्तबईौना अकठरहुमुलखताह } [सूरह अल-अराफ़: 140]. और अल्लाह ने हमें यह आदेश दिया है कि हम अल्लाह के दीन में हमेशा से ही नाफ़िलात करते आए हैं, {वशरअ लकरमिनादीन मावराय } [सूरह अल-अन्कबूत: 43]. और नाफ़िल का अर्थ है अल्लाह के दीन में हमेशा से ही नाफ़िलात करना

in_english.name: Naafil
in_english.meaning: good deeds, acts of virtue, voluntary acts of worship
in_english.long_meaning: Naafil acts: These are the good deeds that are not obligatory, but are recommended by Allah, as mentioned in the Quran: {Fear not those who disbelieve, and grieve not at their plots} [Quran 3:160]. The meaning of Naafil is to do good deeds that are not obligatory, but are recommended by Allah, as mentioned in the Quran: {Shall We treat those who believe and do good like the mischief-makers in the earth? Or shall We treat the righteous like the wrong-doers?} [Quran 38:28]. The term Naafil is used in the Quran to describe the good deeds that are not obligatory, but are recommended by Allah: {And strive in the way of Allah with the effort and resources that are best} [Quran 22:78]. Naafil is also used to describe the good deeds that are done voluntarily, without any expectation of reward: {And strive for the cause of Allah with the effort and resources that are best} [Quran 61:13].
